subject: General Science
title: Waves

outcomes.text: explain the terms used in waves,
interpret the wave equation as used in science,
calculate the wave characteristics using the wave equation,
demonstrate the effects of properties of waves in real life,
appreciate the applications of waves in real life.

content: Application of properties of waves in real life.
inquiry_questions: How are waves applicable in our day-to-day life?
How do waves affect our environment?
suggested_learning_experiences: Use print or non-print media to research on the terms used in waves and properties of waves (wavelength, period, amplitude, frequency and velocity).
Discuss with peers the interpretation of the wave equation by relating the characteristics of the wave.
Solve numerical problems on wave characteristics using the wave equation.
Carry out experiments to investigate reflection of sound waves using the echo method.
Watch video clips on refraction of sound waves both during the day and night and illustrate the concept diagrammatically.
Carry out experiments to establish that sound waves can be heard round a corner.
Search for information on the effect of waves on the environment (communities, marine ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).
Discuss with peers the mitigation measures of the effects of waves on the environment.
Search for information on the applications of waves in day-to-day life such as safe road use (reflection, refraction and diffraction) and discuss with peers.
coreCompetencies:
Learning to learn: as the learner searches for information on applications of reflection, refraction and diffraction of waves.
Critical thinking and problem solving: as the learner searches for information on mitigation measures of the effects of waves on the environment (communities, ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).
values: Unity: as the learners play different roles when carrying out experiments to investigate reflection of sound waves using the echo method.
pcis:
Safety and security: as the learner appreciates some of the applications of waves related to safety in transport.
Environmental issues: as the learner searches for information on the effect of waves on the environment (communities, marine ecosystems, infrastructure and operations).

notes: No lesson allocation is stated in this table; do not use the inventory baseline count as an official allocation.

Echo and sound-diffraction investigations should use moderate sound levels, safe locations and avoid hearing risk. Video/simulation or supplied observations can substitute where a safe echo site is unavailable.
The source's day/night sound-refraction and environmental-impact claims need accurate, appropriately qualified explanations and should not be overstated from a single local observation.
